# localmelo

> localmelo is a local personal agent that runs tasks with tools (shell, Python, files, MCP servers) and memory on a model server the user runs (oMLX, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server) or on a cloud API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, NVIDIA). It offers the `melo` command, which returns a fixed exit code per run and prints one JSON line with `--output-format json`, an experimental Python API, and an HTTP gateway on 127.0.0.1. It is pre-alpha: interfaces may change before v0.1.0.

- Command words (only as the first argument, exact match; a task that starts with one is quoted or follows `--`; one command word after options and no `--` exits 2, saying where it goes): `melo setup` = `--reconfigure`, `melo serve [-p N] [--host H] [--playground] [--force]` = `--serve [--port N] [--host H] [--enable-playground] [--allow-unconfigured]`, `melo serve install|uninstall|status` = `--daemon ACTION`, `melo console [--reset]` = `--gateway-login` / `--gateway-rotate-token`, `melo worker BRIEF [--parent ID] [--title T]` = `--brief BRIEF [--parent-run ID] [--save-session T]`, `melo import FORMAT FILE` = `--import-session FORMAT FILE`, `melo task VERB` = `melo-task VERB`, `melo config` shows the config file and what differs from the defaults. Letters and short names: `-m/--model` = `--chat-model`, `-u/--url` = `--base-url`, `-s/--steps` = `--max-steps`, `-o/--output` = `--output-format`, `--mcp` = `--mcp-config`, `-w` = `--workspace`, `-t` = `--timeout`, `-y` = `--yolo`, `-V` = `--version`; `--title T` = `--save-session T`. Every old spelling keeps working and parses to the same result (launchers, the benchmark and the macOS app need no change). `melo -h` is 23 lines (the everyday options and `setup`, `serve`, `console` with what each does); `melo -h all` (also plain `-h` with `[ui] mode = "developer"` or `--developer`) lists every option, command and setting; `melo COMMAND -h` explains one command. Table: [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#old-spelling-to-new). Tiers: [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#default-and-developer-mode).
- Settings: `-X KEY=VALUE` (or `--set KEY=VALUE`, repeatable, before `--`) changes one `config.toml` key for one run and never writes the file; KEY is `section.name` (`retrieval.k`; `request_timeout_s` has no section), the value is TOML (`true`, `5`, `"v3"`) else text, and `on`/`off` mean booleans. A key with an old option becomes that option before parsing (`-X retrieval.k=5` = `--recall-k 5`, same checks and requests); another key (`cli.stream`, `scheduler.policy`) overrides the loaded config; a bad value or unknown key exits 2 (an unknown key that is an option's name gets the option: `agent.max_steps` is `-s N (--steps)`). `melo config keys [FILTER]`, `melo config get KEY` and `melo config set KEY VALUE` list, read and save keys; nine keys are for one run only (`agent.attempt_policy`, `agent.reflection_gate`, `agent.tool_exposure`, `memory.dir`, `memory.keep_decision_text`, `retrieval.extra_body`, `endpoint.embedding_url`, `endpoint.embedding_model`, `endpoint.reasoning_field`). Old option = key: `--attempt-policy` = `agent.attempt_policy`; `--reflection-gate` = `agent.reflection_gate`; `--fixed-prefix` = `agent.fixed_prefix`; `--window-eviction` = `agent.window_eviction`; `--reflect-tool-guard` = `agent.reflect_tool_guard`; `--cache-layout` = `agent.cache_layout`; `--window-messages` = `agent.window_messages`; `--brief-items` = `agent.brief_items`; `--reasoning` = `agent.reasoning`; `--replay-turns` = `agent.replay_turns`; `--note-writer` = `agent.note_writer`; `--captured-history` = `agent.captured_history`; `--context-window` = `agent.context_window`; `--output-reserve` = `agent.output_reserve`; `--safety-margin` = `agent.safety_margin`; `--tool-exposure` = `agent.tool_exposure`; `--retriever` = `retrieval.retriever`; `--recall-at` = `retrieval.recall_at`; `--recall-k` = `retrieval.k`; `--recall-kinds` = `retrieval.kinds`; `--recall-placement` = `retrieval.placement`; `--recall-min-score` = `retrieval.min_score`; `--retrieval-extra-body` = `retrieval.extra_body`; `--admit-on-outcome` = `memory.admit_on_outcome`; `--keep-decision-text` = `memory.keep_decision_text`; `--memory-dir` = `memory.dir`; `--request-timeout` = `request_timeout_s`; `--no-save-session` = `sessions.record_direct`; `--embedding-base-url` = `endpoint.embedding_url`; `--embedding-model` = `endpoint.embedding_model`; `--reasoning-field` = `endpoint.reasoning_field`. Table: [Settings](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#settings).
- Install from a clone named `localmelo` with Python 3.11+: `uv sync --extra gateway`, then run `uv run melo` in the clone (`melo` is not on PATH). MIT license. localmelo never downloads, starts or serves models.
- One task: `melo --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --chat-model MODEL --output-format json --timeout 300 -- "TASK"`; `--reasoning legacy|drop|replay|compress|compress+replay` (default `legacy`, unchanged) chooses whether a reply's reasoning is sent back, with `--reasoning-field auto|reasoning_content|reasoning` (replay and compress+replay), `--replay-turns N` and `--note-writer auto|heuristic` (compress modes: each reply becomes a RAM-only note and its drafts), `--retriever auto|off|bm25|llm|embedding`, `--recall-at start,attempt,step,tool`, `--recall-k 1..10`, `--recall-kinds note,draft,thought,digest,reflection,long`, `--recall-placement tool|message`, `--recall-min-score 0..1`, `--retrieval-extra-body JSON`, `--admit-on-outcome on|off` and `--keep-decision-text` (R6-lite's typed long store: a candidate is admitted by rehearsal, a user request (which also admits the fact after its marker) or statement, or the outcome switch; one decision per action; `--keep-decision-text` is refused in the UI), and `long_term.db` `user_version` 1 with the typed columns and `decisions` (legacy migrates in place, rows and search unchanged); `melo-retrieve --export-store DIR|FILE`, `--export-decisions DIR|FILE`, `--route CANDIDATES.jsonl --memory-dir DIR` (one action line per input; an optional `task_key` is stored in the digest's provenance, and `REFUSED` means a boundary or admission refusal) score the store offline (a directory with no store prints zero and exits 0); R5: compress recalls at start/attempt/step by default; auto = embedding if configured, else llm at start/attempt and bm25 at step/tool; tool is never on unless named; a step's recall can include a superseded note or thought chunk of an evicted turn, and `memory_stats.recall_empty` counts a recall that found nothing; legacy refuses these flags); `--workspace DIR` makes the run work in that folder: file tools stay inside it and `shell_exec`/`python_exec` start there (default: the current folder; a path that is not a folder exits 2 with one line); a direct run offers `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, and `--builtins all` adds `shell_exec` (off by default) and `list_files`, `--builtins shell_exec` only the shell; exit 0 completed, 1 crashed or a configuration error, 2 any other status or a usage error. Bare `melo` in a terminal opens the interactive UI (a first run asks for a model server and model and saves them, as `ollama` when the server answers `GET /api/version` like Ollama, else as `vllm`; thinking, tool calls and progress shown live, approvals (with a diff for an overwritten file), `/help` (the everyday commands; `/help all` every one), `/model`, `/backend`, `/verbose`, `/thinking`, `/stream`, `/expand`, `/progress`, `/approvals`, `/status` (five rows: model and whether it answers, folder, session, approvals in words, context use; `/status all` adds the tools, memory, limits and the cache, context, steps and tasks rows built from events already received, `--` where a server reports no `cached_tokens`), `/mcp`, `/retry`); `--mcp-config FILE` or the config's top-level `mcp_config` loads MCP servers; without a TTY it exits 2. `melo --serve` starts the gateway (`--port 0`: a free port, printed at startup). A first run marks models the server reports as loaded (oMLX `GET /v1/models/status`, Ollama `GET /api/ps`) and defaults to the first loaded chat model. With several chat models and none known loaded (a 401 or no status route, or none in memory) there is no default: the prompt asks for a number or id, a piped empty answer exits 2, and `melo --base-url URL` without `--chat-model` (the UI, a task, `--brief` or `melo ""`) first lists the server's models and uses the only chat model or the loaded one; several and none known loaded exits 2 listing the models (a 401 from the status route adds a line saying the server needs a key; pass `--chat-model <id>`; `--brief`: a `startup_error` result with `exit_code` 2); a list that cannot be read keeps `default`, with a stderr warning in text output. Agents: do not run bare `melo` in a pty under the user's HOME, and use direct mode in scripts.
- arm64 macOS development app, signed ad hoc: `uv run python scripts/build_macos_app.py --install` builds it into `~/Applications/LocalMelo.app` (replaced only when its bundle id is `org.localmelo.app`) and links `~/.local/bin/melo` only when no other `melo` is on `PATH`; `--uninstall` removes both and nothing else; see [macOS app](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/macos-app.md); the page instance check is not authentication, it checks the port owner and the instance before sending any login code, binds the code to that instance, starts its gateway with `--port 0` and reads the port from the startup line `Gateway: http://127.0.0.1:PORT` (20 s start deadline); its window shows a native starting view and, when the gateway cannot start or stops, an in-window failure with Try Again, Open Log and Quit (no dialog, the app stays open); it signs its web view in using one-use gateway login codes, offers "Sign in again" after a token rotation, and quit always asks and names what would stop; the menu-bar item is the localmelo logo (`docs/assets/icon_small.png`, in colour, not a template image) with the running count beside it and a red dot while `status.waiting` (chats and tasks with an approval to answer) is not empty, its "Waiting for your approval" entry opens that chat or task, and the build renders the app icon from `docs/assets/melo.png` (the whole emblem on a rounded tile of its own paper colour, every size resampled from the source, with `numpy` and `iconutil`); the build leaves tkinter, turtle, IDLE, pip, setuptools, ensurepip and 2to3 out of the bundled Python (`UNUSED` in the script, 36 MB), so `python_exec` under the app's `melo` cannot import them; the window, Dock and menus call the app localmelo, and `LocalMelo.app` is only the file name. `/api/health` `sessions.store_reason` distinguishes `owned`, `open-error`, `failed` and healthy `null`.
- Provider `stream_chat` yields provisional raw fragments and a completed reply; close on early exit, never persist raw deltas. `StreamFilter` buffers without a framing declaration; a trusted `reasoning_tags` hint allows line-level redacted release (an open PEM private key block is held until its END line, or past 16 KiB its body is dropped as it arrives). Only the interactive UI consumes it, and it does by default (`[cli] stream = true` is the default; `-X cli.stream=false` for one run, `melo config set cli.stream false` for good) with per-model `[cli.reasoning_tags]` (`explicit`, `closing_only`, `none`) and `/stream on|off` (`/new` resets it to `[cli] stream`; `[cli] status_line = "auto"|"off"` (default auto, no flag) adds `cache`, `ctx`, `tasks` and, in developer mode, `step` segments to the bottom bar from events already received, dropped right to left on a narrow terminal); a server that ignores `stream` (one JSON body) or ends the stream before any delta is read as a whole reply (`OpenAICompatLLM` asks once more without `stream` in the second case, marks the reply `StreamFragment.whole`, and does not ask that server to stream again; the UI prints `This server sends replies whole; melo shows them when they are complete.` once), while a stream that breaks after a delta keeps `Streaming response ended before completion`; released text shows in the live area, provisional text prints once to scrollback labelled, the final answer prints once, and only that UI streams; an invalid `[cli]` value warns instead of failing a run. [provider reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/python-api.md#custom-model-providers).
- Fixed prefix is the default: `[agent] fixed_prefix = false` or `--fixed-prefix off` sends the earlier requests, `--fixed-prefix on|off` overrides the config. Local date and UTC offset freeze per run; `fixed-prefix-v2` puts the latest reflection last under `cache_layout v2` and makes a reflection request repeat the latest plan request (same tools) plus one final user message; `all` freezes sorted schemas while `retrieve` remains dynamic. `prefix_cache.schema_changes` counts changes, not measured server misses; cached tokens appear only when reported for planning/reflection.
- Window eviction: `[agent] window_eviction = "chunk"|"boundary"|"slide"` or `--window-eviction`. `chunk` (default) drops down to 12 messages, and the prompt-cap fit and the `--context-window` fit down to 70% of their limit, keeping the cut until a request passes the limit; `boundary` also drops a finished attempt at the next attempt; `slide` drops one unit per step once the 20-message window is full. Modes other than `slide` add `config.window_eviction` to the JSON result.
- Cache layout (default `v3`): `[agent] cache_layout = "v2"|"v3"` or `--cache-layout`. `v3` with the fixed prefix appends a reflection once at the attempt boundary as a window message, keeps the reflection request and reply in the window, and retries an unreadable reflection on the same prefix; `v2` (the earlier requests) rebuilds the reflection as the last message of every plan request; no effect without the fixed prefix. `--window-messages N` / `[agent] window_messages` (8-256) is the window's message cap: default 64 on a local server and for `--base-url`, 20 on a cloud vendor; a value you set wins; under `chunk`/`boundary` the prompt-size fit evicts in chunks. `--cache-layout v2 --window-messages 20` send the earlier requests. `config.cache_layout` is in the JSON result unless `v2`, `config.window_messages` unless 20.
- `--reflect-tool-guard on|off` (default `on`; `[agent] reflect_tool_guard = false` also turns it off): on makes every reflection request offer the tools of that step's planning request and end with `Answer with the JSON object only; do not call any tool.`; `tool_choice` and the retry are unchanged. The `reflection` event's `unreadable_reason` is `tool_call`, `invalid`, `no_json` or `null`.
- Reflection reading (default `reflection_gate=flags`, no option): a reply with no reflection as it stands gets one repair of a `{...}` the decoder rejects (the first 8 per reply): drop the `]` or `}` at the error that no opener matches (`unmatched_closer`), a comma before a closer (`trailing_comma`), escape raw newline, carriage return and tab characters in strings (`control_char`), double the backslash of an `Invalid \escape` (`invalid_escape`), or insert a `]` before the comma that precedes the key at which the decoder stopped inside an array (`unclosed_array`); it counts only with a valid `recommended_action`, two repairs (a second invalid escape included) or text that stops short stay unreadable. The `reflection` event's `repaired` names it, else `null`. A retry after `invalid` or `no_json` with rejected JSON adds the line `Your reply was not valid JSON (<error> at character <n>: ...<up to 60 characters>...). Reply again with one JSON object.` after the retry note; `tool_call` and `--reflection-gate utility` are unchanged.
- The cache settings are the defaults of direct runs, the interactive UI, the gateway and `AgentOptions()`; `--fixed-prefix off --window-eviction slide --reflect-tool-guard off` (hidden from default help, listed by `melo --developer --help`) send the earlier requests byte for byte. A config key you set stays, a missing key is the default, saving writes a key only when it differs. The JSON result gains `prefix_cache` and `config.window_eviction`, `config.reflect_tool_guard` by default.
- Cache telemetry: the `usage` of `assistant.message` and `reflection` events also has `cached_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` when the server sent them (streamed with `stream_options.include_usage` too; absent means not reported, never 0; summed over a reflection's requests), and `prefix` (`null` for a run's first request, else `{messages, chars, against: {kind, request}, previous_messages, total_messages, first_changed, tools_changed, fresh_chars, request_chars}`: how much of the best earlier plan or reflect request of the run this one repeats, and the role of the first message that changed; on `reflection` it is for its first request). Request bodies and the JSON result are unchanged. `python scripts/cache_report.py LOG` prints one row per request (kind plan or reflect) from a `stream-json` log, then totals by kind and overall and a `reusable` line (`cached / (prompt - fresh)`, `fresh` estimated from `prefix.fresh_chars` / `prefix.request_chars`, which also hold the characters no earlier request of the run had). See docs/reference/events.md.
- `--brief-items on|off` (experimental, default off; `[agent] brief_items = true`): with `--brief`, reflection requests and the check two steps before the last attempt ends list the brief's numbered items no edit has touched yet (marks from `git status`; edits only, never "done"); each use emits a `brief_items` notice.
- Captured history is opt-in via `[agent] captured_history = true` or `--captured-history on`; `off` overrides config. The separate history copy is pattern-redacted and capped at 200,000 characters per result; acquisition omissions are unknown. Model previews use a 50,000-character limit. Redaction can miss secrets.
- Lean output (experimental, default off, no flag): `[agent] lean_output = true` or `-X agent.lean_output=true`. For a task given on the command line (`melo "TASK"`, `--brief`, `melo worker BRIEF`, `json` and `stream-json` too) only; the `melo ""` loop, the interactive UI and the gateway ignore it. The system prompt's last line `Think step by step. Be concise.` is replaced by: no text between tool calls, a final answer of at most three lines, relative paths without `sys.path` setup, read the files a task names before listing folders. With `reflection_gate flags` the reflection prompt drops `progress_made`, `new_information_gained` and the five estimates and asks for `best_effort_result` only with `done` or `stop`; `utility` keeps the full prompt. Off, requests are unchanged.
- Context accounting is opt-in: set `[agent] context_window`, `output_reserve`, `safety_margin`, or matching flags, all positive with window > reserve + margin. It fits over-budget planning/reflection requests on a copy, or ends `context_budget_exceeded`; it does not enforce a generation cap. Estimates, including the image allowance, are not bounds. See [configuration](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md#context-accounting).
- Reasoning/recall in sessions: interactive flags `--reasoning`, `--reasoning-field`, `--replay-turns`, `--note-writer`, `--retriever`, `--recall-*`, `--retrieval-extra-body` override `[agent]`/`[retrieval]` defaults; a `--base-url` session ignores those defaults. Native Ollama refuses an explicit reasoning-field flag. Console sessions honor configured reasoning (default `legacy`) while keeping gateway tool mode; legacy `/v1` is unchanged. `/model`/`/backend` keep mode/conversation and RAM-only notes/drafts; replay-required drop refusal retains the old Agent and MCP state. Session replay scope is window; pairs restore no old thinking, window restores retained redacted thinking; current mode wins over old outcome config. Notes remain RAM-only, not restored from turns.note. `[agent] tool_env` lists extra inherited shell/Python variable names (valid ASCII names, missing skipped, save names only); SSH_AUTH_SOCK grants SSH-agent access and proxy variables may expose credentials. Defaults expose nothing new; --base-url ignores it; MCP env is separate. See [configuration](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md#tool-environment).
- Attempt digests skip task headings; `verified` requires a passing test runner or a check referencing an earlier written file. A failed last check removes verification. Python check labels use a recognized runner and safe target basename, or a neutral label; Python writes are not inferred as `files`; hidden paths and agent scratch notes are omitted. Results use counts, exit code or `completed`, not arbitrary output.
- `melo-task` controls tasks through an authenticated loopback gateway: new, list, show, pause, resume, stop, level and follow (`stop` prints `stop requested; …` until the state is `cancelled`; poll `show`). `new --brief FILE` or `--stdin` supplies untrusted content; retry ambiguous creation with the same request key. `--json` returns versioned JSON/NDJSON; default follow prints one readable line per event (time, type, summary) and list prints an aligned table with a header. `follow --wait` maps done/failed/cancelled-or-expired to 0/1/2; the terminal line adds the event-completeness caveat only after a reconnect or `--after` skip, and a quiet follow is not proof of complete replay. A task held on a tool approval lists it in `pending_approvals` (`GET /api/tasks`), `show` prints `Waiting for your approval: <tool> <target>`, and `POST /api/approvals/{request_id}` or the console Tasks view answers it.
- `--brief FILE` runs a bounded UTF-8 worker brief with a versioned JSON result; `--output-format stream-json` emits NDJSON events followed by a result. Agent construction errors, including refused config values and invalid TOML, report `startup_error`; output failures attempt `transport_error` but may prevent any final record. A broken startup-output pipe exits 1. Drain stdout, check exit and final result; startup error text is redacted and `$HOME` appears as `~`; a brief run appends a fixed worker-protocol paragraph to the brief, continues after any `continue` reflection whatever its flags say while steps and attempts remain, and adds a `no_change` notice plus a "Nothing has changed in the workspace yet" line at an attempt boundary where a git workspace is unchanged (ending with "Start with: <first next direction>"), the same notice with `scope: "step"` plus a "You have read for 6 steps…" line after 6 steps in a row without a workspace change, a tail note of tool output the window dropped (newest 8) on each planning request, and a reflection request that asks for paths with line numbers and the first command to run next (none of this without `--brief`); a brief's lines that start with `Check:` (rest of line = one shell command) are run by the harness as `shell_exec` calls (run in every `--builtins` setting, the model's own `shell_exec` calls unchanged; `--workspace` root and timeout apply) before the run ends `completed`: a failing check sends the model back with its command, exit code and last 60 output lines, at most twice (also once with exactly two steps of the last attempt left, when the workspace changed since the checks last ran), and the result's `tests` is `passed` or `failed` (items `source: "brief_check"` with `output_tail`: last 20 output lines, redacted, ≤4,000 chars; also `failed` when refused or still failing; the run still ends `completed`, exit 4 and a stderr line) with `brief_check` and `brief_check_failed` notices; explicit `--inbox FILE` reads complete instruction lines at planning boundaries and `inbox.accepted` offsets confirm live context insertion, not model receipt or cross-crash replay; `--inbox-fd N` reads the same lines from an inherited pipe whose read end is close-on-exec before tools start, so python, shell and MCP subprocesses cannot write it (recommended for untrusted tasks). A file inbox inside the workspace is refused as `setup_error` (exit 2, no model call); a file inbox is a steering channel, not a trust boundary, and same-user processes and tools can still write elsewhere. Acknowledgements wait for a slow reader instead of being dropped. Saved event text is redacted; session resume does not replay it. Redaction is pattern-based; arbitrary secrets may remain.
- Episodic digest recall prefers the same normalized task and workspace realpath; keyless digests are cross-task. `[retrieval]` has `cross_task_ratio = 1.1`, `cross_task_cap = 1` and `cross_task_cold = 0` (1 permits one cold cross-task digest). General memories bypass this gate. A digest without a checked `files:` or `verified:` line is not admitted; a later evidence-less attempt does not drop an earlier evidence-bearing attempt's digest. Delivered recall records and run stats report long-digest same/cross counts plus a task-local note count.
- Compress-mode heuristic notes extract up to 12 facts from visible replies without a note block, including bounded English negative/cancellation and Chinese residence/cancellation forms verbatim. Negative attribution requires the full assertion in the record; conflicting event times reject a match. This is heuristic: similar opposing detected polarities conflict rather than deduplicate; structured supersession is off by default. Python-only `AgentOptions(typed_assertions=True)` opts into narrow evidence-checked same-task updates and labelled historical recall; order comes from a timezone-aware record `timestamp`/`date` or per-task user message and sentence position (a restart does not link earlier user statements), only exact normalized duplicates stay ignored (different near-duplicates are kept), recall order uses wall-clock time, unlinked assertions remain unlinked and recall is relevance-limited. See [Memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/memory.md#reasoning-notes).
- Worker sessions: every direct run records one turn by default (`--no-save-session` or `[sessions] record_direct = false` opts out; `--save-session TITLE` titles it; `--parent-run ID` links a launcher); the web console Workers view follows an unfinished run on its event stream. `--import-session dsh-jsonl FILE [--title TITLE]` imports once by content hash. Read via `GET /api/sessions?kind=worker` (filters `status`, `source`, `parent_run`; `cursor` / `next_cursor`) and worker detail/turns, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events` (follows an unfinished run by polling the file about once a second) and `/status`; no writes. `GET /api/sessions?kind=terminal` lists the chats of interactive `melo` sessions of the same file, read-only, served by id as worker runs are, with `kind` `terminal` and every text redacted on read (the terminal stores a chat unredacted); write routes return 404 for them. Workspace defaults to cwd; `session.tokens` is total tokens, `meta.usage` is the usage map; SQLite may create WAL/SHM sidecars on reads. Regex redaction is not a guarantee against arbitrary printed secrets; recognizable sensitive file reads are omitted. Thinking follows session retention.
- The web workspace offers `#/tasks` (task list) and `#/tasks/<id>` (card with state, recovery card as text, evidence status, Resume with a confirmation dialog only after 409 `confirmation_required`, task Stop via `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}` `{"state":"stop"}`, and "Start again as a new task" when a started task has no card). See the console guide.
- The web workspace offers `#/workers` (server-filtered and cursor-paged) and `#/workers/<id>` (read-only; an open unfinished run is read once and followed on `/events`, the list re-read every 3 s, no write controls; a Terminal chats chip lists `kind=terminal` chats, followed while a turn runs and again at the next turn). A started task's card in `#/tasks/<id>` shows a Live section: its session (the task id) read once with `/turns?events=true`, then a running or held task followed on `/events?after=<last id>` (a hidden tab closes the stream, a shown one resumes; it closes after one last read when the task is done, failed, cancelled, expired, interrupted or parked); task events are shown as a chat's are, unredacted. Worker detail `tokens` is null without integer completion tokens; chat-only details and submission lookup return 404 for worker-only IDs. See the console guide and API v2 reference below.
- The `/` workspace shows a setup card while no model can answer and no chat is open: it calls `GET /api/setup/detect` (the first run's detection; `state` `found`|`needs_key`|`none`, `name`, `backend`, chat `models`, `loaded`, `suggested` (null: the user chooses), `problem`) only while shown, and Use this model saves through `PUT /api/settings` (a `vllm` backend whose listing named oMLX is written `omlx`), tests and reads health; the composer is disabled meanwhile. It uses `/api` for connection settings, connection testing, a browser-local theme, tools/grants/memory/runs drawer (developer mode, saved as `[ui] mode` from the settings' Developer tab, adds an Events tab, memory internals and run counters; display only), earlier turns, failure controls and per-tab outbox recovery; its styles are tokens in `workspace.css` `:root` (colour as `light-dark()` pairs, a type scale with a 12px floor, four radii) that `tests/gateway/test_web_assets.py` enforces; console sessions use `RememberingPolicy` to ask before `file_write` and `python_exec` and render approval cards (`Allow once`, `Allow for this chat`, `Deny` + note; body unchanged); a failed turn offers one next action per status (a model server that cannot be reached: `Could not reach the model server`, Try again, a `Change the server address` link, its raw error only under Details); Escape stops a running turn only with focus in the composer and closes what is open in every view; default mode (`[ui] mode` not `developer`, read from `GET /api/settings` at boot) hides, keeping every id, the level chip, Details, the GPU line, the LOCAL badge, the status row's cache, step, phase and queue segments, the task priority and the Workers and Tasks links until a run, terminal chat or task exists, names the model in the header chip, shows a banner while a chat waits on a foreign GPU lock (its turn reads `Waiting for this Mac's GPU` in both modes) and stacks the settings dialog (Model with its test, Appearance, Developer toggle); a new chat shows a folder chip (`#folder-btn`, `In <folder>`; the default is `GET /api/settings` `workspace`) with a panel of the default, up to four recent folders and Choose a folder (a path field in a browser; in the macOS app the `localmeloFolder` message handler's system panel) and one-line starters (`#starters`), and `POST /api/sessions` carries the pick as `workspace` (absent for the default); a chat's header and sidebar row name its folder, an accent dot marks a chat waiting for approval, and on a phone or touch screen the keyboard hints and the model chip (while it only names the model) are hidden and a failed turn's next steps are 44 px buttons; developer mode shows all as before; legacy `/v1` has no approval policy.
- Saved terminal chats: `melo -c` resumes the newest eligible chat in this workspace; `melo -r [ID|TITLE]`, `/sessions [filter]` and `/resume [id|title]` resolve or pick one. Picker filtering, Tab folder/all-folders and Esc preserve the draft. Startup selection precedes the banner; the recap names the chosen chat. Exit prints `melo -c` when the chat is the newest of the folder melo ran in, else `melo -r ID`. Resuming keeps current model/workspace and `/verbose`/`/thinking`, clears grants and explains restored memory (`[sessions] resume_mode = "pairs"` default or `"window"`); `/retry` keeps stored typed text and `/expand` reads persisted tool output. Cross-window changes reload before sending; busy/deleted sessions keep drafts. Only CLI chats with finished turns are offered; no web/scheduler sessions. `-c` and `-r` are mutually exclusive and interactive-only. Direct parsing/output stays unchanged; put task text after `--`.
- Interactive text attachments: `/attach PATH` (quote spaces), `/attachments`, `/detach N|all`; explicitly select an `@` file completion, not typed prose. Idle only; detach before switching sessions. Workspace regular UTF-8 text only: no symlinks, traversal, URLs, recognized secret files, binary or images. Max 8, 256 KiB each, 512 KiB total original bytes; composed prompt limit also applies. Redaction is best effort; changed snapshots are shown for confirmation. Session snapshots are stored unencrypted; `/retry` uses the stored snapshot, not the file. Pairs resume has a 32,000-character user/answer budget and may omit a turn; window can omit it too. See [terminal guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md#attach-text-files).
- Interactive `! COMMAND` (idle only): runs COMMAND in `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh` as the user in the workspace with the terminal handed over (Ctrl+C/Esc go to the child). Not a sandbox: no approval, checker or policy; it can leave the workspace. Output stays in the terminal: never in model context, history or events, and the command is not saved in input history. `/attach !` attaches a redacted snapshot (last 256 KiB, minus concealed text and anything before a screen clear, a cut start loses its partial first line) to the next message: it always prints the exact snapshot and asks `[y/N]`, default No; once attached it is stored with the session, unencrypted, like `/attach PATH`. `!` alone shows help; `\! text` sends a literal leading `! `. Refused (draft kept) during a turn, approval, switch or another command. melo exit sends SIGTERM, terminal hangup SIGHUP, then SIGKILL after 2 s, to the child's own process group only. Not in direct mode or the plain loop. See [terminal guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md#run-a-shell-command).
- Terminal session tools: `/title [text]` shows/sets a title (kept until lazy first-turn creation); idle-only `/undo` forgets the newest finished turn, keeps typed history and never reverses file changes; a committed undo reports success even after Esc, and `/retry` re-runs that undone turn without undoing the previous one. `/usage` includes undone work, leaves missing/running counters unknown and reflows on narrow terminals; `/memory` inspects a copied, cleaned working window and explains the actual resume mode, without model calls or memory writes. `/copy [turn]` copies stored redacted Markdown without thinking, preserving indentation/newlines with bounded turn reads, not wrapped terminal output; local macOS uses bounded `/usr/bin/pbcopy`, SSH/other platforms/failure request OSC 52 (terminal support varies). Tests must fake native copying: temporary HOME does not isolate the OS clipboard.
- Tools run with the user's permissions and no sandbox; `python_exec` code runs in a child process, killed at its time limit. The gateway requires a bearer or browser session and refuses non-loopback binds; same-UID processes and services on other localhost ports are not isolated by file permissions or cookie names. Only `interactive` mode offers `shell_exec` by default; a direct run and the Python API's default `mode="python"` register `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, the gateway and a console session add the read-only `list_files` (as `interactive` does), and `--builtins all` (or naming `shell_exec`) turns the shell on in a direct run or the Python API, after which it runs without an approval unless that run passes `approval=` (a `python`-mode run can). `AgentOptions(mode="direct"|"interactive"|"gateway"|"python")`; an explicit `builtins` set always wins, except that a gateway still refuses `shell_exec`, named or not.

- Gateway security-1b is in progress: `/v1/playground/*` is disabled (404) by default; `melo --serve --enable-playground` opts in behind authentication and Host/Origin checks, using the saved local backend/model rather than per-request endpoints or models. Authenticated settings/model probes accept typed absolute HTTP/HTTPS URLs and do not follow redirects. Explicit session close/delete refuses a running or queued start with 409, without cancelling the run (`session_busy` on `/api`). Console delete can also return a transient `session_busy` while maintenance holds the session lock; retry.

- `[gateway] workspace` is empty (console default `~/localmelo-workspace`) or an absolute/`~/` path that must not resolve to `/` or home.

## Docs

- [localmelo for agents](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/for-agents.md): the one page an agent needs: install, CLI, Python API, HTTP, results, config, tools, memory, gotchas and rules.
- [Quickstart](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/start/quickstart.md): install, run a first task, save a configuration and start the gateway.
- [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md): `melo` modes, options, output, exit codes and signals; [interactive UI guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md) covers keys, commands and approvals.
- [Run results](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/run-results.md): run statuses, the fields of the JSON line and `RunResult`, and retries.
- [Python API](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/python-api.md): `Agent`, `AgentOptions`, `RunResult` and methods; [Python guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/python.md) covers stopping, approvals and workspaces.
- [Events](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/events.md): the events a Python run reports, their order, fields and rules. The `reflection` event carries `flags` (the decision's three booleans), `gate`, `utility` and `stop_reason` (null iff `continue_run`; else `unreadable_reply`, `action_not_continue`, `no_attempt_left`, `step_budget_used`, `not_feasible`, `not_concrete`, `not_novel` or `utility_below_threshold`).
- [Session guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/sessions.md) and [sessions reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/sessions.md): conversations kept in SQLite (experimental Python API): turns, statuses, message ids, resume, approvals for a person and the event stream; `SessionRunner(..., progress=True)` stores a turn's `run.progress`, `run_turn`/`start_turn` take `routine=`, and `build_session_agent` can wrap the providers the Agent is built with (`wrap_llm`/`wrap_embedding`).
- [Gateway guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/gateway.md), [web console](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/web-console.md) and [HTTP v1 reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/http-v1.md): startup, loopback guard, workspace and legacy routes.
- [API v2](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/api-v2.md): the web console's `/api` routes (health, whose `status` counts what runs now by kind (chats, tasks, runs, terminal chats) with a capped `items` list for the header's `N running` chip, settings, key-status, connection test, model listing, `GET /api/setup/detect` (the model server on this Mac), sessions, turns, SSE events, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/status` (the terminal's developer-mode status-bar segments, compact, and numbers for a chat or task session; `cache --`, never 0%, when no cached tokens are reported; worker runs too), blobs, submission lookups, the writes that create a session and start, retry, stop and approve its turns, its scheduler level and typing heartbeat, scheduler task creation, inspection and control, and the details: tools, grants, memory and runs), the one error shape, the 1 MiB body limit and JSON content-type rule, a [create-run-approve script](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/api-client.md), and the additive-only promise; loopback only. S3a.2 task workers: they share the gate, disable memory, omit `shell_exec`, and have at most four resident workers. Rows survive restart; startup interrupts uncertain tasks and preserves verified parked cards without replay. Recovered tasks stay fenced from `PATCH` resume and priority changes until `POST /api/tasks/{id}/resume` `{operation_id, confirmation_token?}` (202 `{task, operation_id}`; an operation ID names one operation, so a retry returns the committed row whatever its payload, and returns 409 once its turn started after a restart). A proved never-started parked or interrupted task queues as its first start with no card or confirmation (a queued never-started create is admitted by startup, not this route; every create records that proof in its own transaction, before any launch); a started task resumes free only with a valid card, trusted complete capture and every recorded group verifiably gone (a verified boot change counts as gone only on the host that recorded it; another or unknown host is not evidence). Anything else first returns 409 `confirmation_required` with a 300 s single-use in-memory token bound to the task, source execution, evidence and CAS generation. Missing card, invalid workspace, stale identity, terminal state and unresolved recovery operations block Resume (Stop and a new task stay available). Stop always wins, invalidates pending tokens and cancels a queued resumed turn before a worker starts. Inability to verify is never evidence; neither path proves cleanup or exactly-once effects. Orphan verification, deadlines and accounting are deferred. Invalid workspaces fail a run; Resume returns 409 `invalid_transition` and leaves the row interrupted. Pause records pending P5 while running providers and tools finish; a held plan, reflection or undelivered approval can park, save an evidence card and release its slot. Resume uses that card and re-asks withdrawn approvals. A task paused before start starts no worker until resumed. Resume restores prior priority from a durable snapshot or computed P2 without one; an unpaused task returns 409 `not_paused`. Unsaved parks retry with the fence closed, then interrupt with a card; while finalization cannot be stored, resume and stop return 503. Cleanup failure quarantines the worker and retains its slot until restart. PATCH `first` is rejected with 400 until S6b. `request_key` makes creation idempotent.
- [Tools reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/tools.md) and [Tools and MCP guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/tools-mcp.md): built-ins, MCP configuration, permissions and checks.
- [Memory reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/memory.md), [memory guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/memory.md) and [memory concepts](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/memory.md): storage, inspection, reset and the memory layers.
- [Configuration reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/configuration.md), [setup guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/configure.md) and [model servers](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/model-servers.md): wizard, backends and configuration keys; oMLX (recommended on Apple silicon) is the `vllm` backend, which first-run setup saves as `chat_backend = "omlx"`.
- [Set up an embedding model](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/embedding.md): long-term memory's embedding backend, the probe that proves one works, and server commands for Ollama, oMLX, vLLM, SGLang and MLC.
- [Troubleshooting](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/troubleshooting.md): error messages and how to fix them.

## Optional

- [How localmelo works](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/how-it-works.md): the run loop, reflection, memory and timeouts.
- [Evaluations](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/project/evaluations.md): the controlled comparisons behind the defaults, such as the reflection gate (one model, 12 coding exercises).
- [Offline retrieval](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/retrieval.md): `melo-retrieve`, which compares memory retrievers offline; runs do not use it.
- [Procedural memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/procedures.md): the steps of recurring tasks, which every run records at its end (`procedures.db` with persistence on) and which `run.progress` events report to a Python caller and `melo` draws as a progress line on a terminal; `localmelo.support.progress_line.format_past` gives that line's past facts and items alone; `melo-procedures` replays the progress rules offline.
- [Scheduler](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/scheduler.md): the scheduling policy core and its simulator, for maintainers; the gateway's web chats and the console's sessions are gated (`[scheduler] policy`, default `off`), and it reads the shared GPU lock and the battery, holding chats while a foreign session holds the lock under `[scheduler] lock_gate = "wait"` (default `record`, which only records); direct runs and the CLI are unchanged.
- [Developer guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/en/developers.html): the repository layout, the development setup, the tests and checks, adding a backend, a built-in tool or a check, and how to send a change.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): notable changes; there is no release yet, so all are under Unreleased.
- [Repository](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo): source code, issues and the contributing guide.
